findings.title: The 2 mm screen does not remove the dents at the end points of draws 7 and 6, contrary to §0 and §6
findings.detail: §0 says the dents 'disappear at 2 mm and 1 mm mesh'. §6 says 'At 2 mm … L1 resolves the coordinate's sign', and §7 says option A 'removes both mechanisms that trap the search (T3, T5)'. The diagnosis's own T5 rows contradict this. At hmax 2 mm, b₇ and b₆ are still strict local minima along row_LS_u0: both ±0.5 mm steps go uphill. At 1 mm the step toward W* goes downhill, so at 2 mm the sign is wrong. The §3.4 table reports the first step only at 4 and 1 mm, which hides this. Its own sign-change column (3 at 2 mm for draws 7 and 6) shows the ruggedness survives at 2 mm. My recomputation puts the minimum's disappearance between 2 and 1.5 mm. Option A probably still works on these draws, because its line moves (2–16 steps) jump the shallow 2 mm dent (0.016–0.05 %). But the claim that the 2 mm screen removes mechanism (a) is wrong. The reason for choosing 2 mm (resolution of the sign) is not shown, and that choice feeds a founder decision (frozen.proxy.rule, re-deriving W*).
findings.evidence: t5_l1_mesh.json, first step toward W* (k1 − k0) at 4/2/1 mm: draw 7 +0.00206/+0.00016/−0.00112; draw 6 +0.00144/+0.00053/−0.00064. Independent loop_inductance recompute, (−0.5 mm step, +0.5 mm step) in %: hmax 2 mm draw 7 (+0.016, +0.192), draw 6 (+0.053, +0.142); hmax 2.5 mm draw 7 (+0.077, +0.25); hmax 1.5 mm draw 7 (−0.090, +0.146), draw 6 (−0.057, +0.092).
findings.suggested_check: Add the 2 mm first-step column to §3.4. Then either rest the case for option A's screen on line moves alone, or measure end-point local optimality at 1.5 mm, which the T7 cost data can price.

findings.title: Draws 0 and 4 are misattributed: a slot1_u0 / row_LS_u0 coupled DRC wall, not only dents, stops the die-row move
findings.detail: §4 counts draws 0 and 4 as die-row/fidelity misses ('left in a dent'). It says the only coupled block is PHASE/HS/slot2 on draws 2 and 3, and that 'slot1_u0 is not the cause'. In fact, from b₀ and b₄, row_LS_u0 cannot go below 14.0 mm while slot1_u0 stays at its planted 13.0 mm (W* 7.0). Both in_domain ('slot1_free_end') and DRC ('die_edge_margin') reject the move. slot1_u0 single moves are L1-flat (relative change of about 2e-5, slightly uphill), so a search that accepts only strict improvements never unlocks the wall. On draw 0 the only valid row step, 14.5 → 14.0, is L1-uphill at 4 mm (1.0078 → 1.0084), and the wall comes right after it. The E0 and B4 counterfactuals move slot1_u0 by −6 mm for exactly this reason. So mechanism (b) covers four of the six misses, not two, and the per-draw counts are wrong. 'slot1_u0 is not the cause' holds only for L2 pricing (B4b, B5), not for reach. Option A's rule 2 names slot free-end rules, so it plausibly covers this case, but as specified it fires only when a ±0.5 mm single move is rejected. From b₀ the single step is valid but uphill, and on the paired path at 4 mm (1.0078, 1.0084, 1.0078, 1.0084, 1.0074 … 1.0059) the paired steps alternately rise and fall before descending, so at 4 mm draw 0 may stay trapped.
findings.evidence: Validity scan from each end point (common.L1.valid): draw 4 row_LS_u0 17.0 … 14.0 ok (L1 1.0093 → 0.9987), 13.5 … 11.0 drc; draw 0 14.0 ok (1.0084), 13.5 … 11.0 drc. Violation at 13.5: die_edge_margin; in_domain: (False, 'slot1_free_end'). Pair (row_LS_u0, slot1_u0) both −0.5·k from row 14.0, all valid: draw 4 L1 0.9971, 0.9937 … 0.9868; draw 0 1.0078, 1.0084, 1.0074, 1.0066, 1.0060, 1.0059. slot1_u0 −0.5/−1/−2 alone: 1.00782/1.00782/1.00783 (draw 0).
findings.suggested_check: Re-attribute draws 0 and 4 in §4 and §0 as dent plus a slot1 coupled block. State that option A's coupled-move rule must also apply when a line move (n ≥ 2), not just a single move, is rejected.

findings.title: Small wording inaccuracies in the T3c and T4 descriptions
findings.detail: The PHASE-only and partial-pair moves from b₂ fail DRC (min_spacing DC+/PHASE 1.5 mm < 2.0 mm) as well as in_domain 'slot2_free_end'. The text names only the second. D2 is a five-parameter change but is counted among 'one or two structured moves'. On the T5 first steps, 1 mm draw 7 is −0.0011, not −0.0012. None of these changes a conclusion.
findings.evidence: M.check on b₂ with col_PHASE_u0 −0.5: Violation(rule='min_spacing', … 1.500e-03 m < 2.000e-03 m); in_domain (False, 'slot2_free_end'). t5 rows draw 7 1 mm: 1.0037610 → 1.0026374.

findings.title: Counterfactual L2 values exist only at 0.5 mm, and nothing was tested as a full search
findings.detail: Every T4/T6 ratio comes from l2_layout at 0.5 mm, while the objective scores at 0.25 mm. The burst end points agree across levels (draw 4: 1.0416 against s 0.042; draw 7: 1.0338 against 0.034), so the die-row amplifier is not a 0.5 mm artefact for the end points. The six rescue counterfactuals themselves have no 0.25 mm check. §9 acknowledges this and costs the check.
findings.evidence: t4_l2_local.json recomputed from l2/solves/*.json: all 15 ratios match, GMRES flags 0, 144–146 iterations, tol ≤ 1.61e-5, W* local/burst − 1 = 6.7e-15.
findings.suggested_check: Run the 7-fingerprint 0.25 mm job list from §9 before committing to option A's burst.

independent_checks_performed: Recomputed the T5 quadratic-residual RMS, slope sign changes and first steps from the rows of t5_l1_mesh.json. RMS and sign counts reproduce the §3.4 table exactly. The first steps at 2 mm (not reported in §3.4) are uphill for draws 7 and 6.

Called physics.peec.loop_inductance independently at hmax 3, 2.5, 2 and 1.5 mm for b₀, b₄, b₆ and b₇ with ±0.5 mm row_LS_u0 steps. The local minima on draws 7 and 6 persist at 2 mm and disappear at 1.5 mm.
Recomputed all 15 T4 L2 ratios from the raw solve JSONs against local W*. All match t4_l2_local.json and the §3.5 table. GMRES converged (flag 0), and local and burst W* agree to 6.7e-15.
Checked the arithmetic of the per-draw rescues: L2 gains of 2.57–5.63 points to 0.9865–0.9979, and L1 at 4 mm improving for E0, D2, C2, C4, B4 and B3 (all hold).

Independently tested coupled-block validity from b₂ and b₃. col_PHASE_u0 −0.5 alone or with one partner is invalid; the triple at −0.5 and −1.0 is valid. L1 1.0233 → 1.0082 and 1.0554 → 1.0383 reproduced.

Read local._joint and LocalConfig (k uniform on 2..4, choice without replacement over 36 movable parameters, ±, 1..4 steps, n_joint = 12) and re-derived P ≈ (1/3)(1/7140)(1/8)(1/16) ≈ 3.6e-7 per proposal. Claim holds.

Scanned row_LS_u0 line-move validity from b₀, b₄ and b₇, identified the blocking rules (die_edge_margin, slot1_free_end), and tested paired slot1_u0/row_LS_u0 moves and L1 flatness of slot1_u0. This revealed the misattribution of draws 0 and 4.
Checked the §3.2 numbers against t2_fidelity.json (a = 0.711, r = 0.90, 0.48 %/mm, n = 55 gives 0.44, leave-one-out 0.41–0.49). All hold.
Checked the pass counts from the §1 and §3.1 tables: L2 2 of 8, L1 indicator 5 of 8. Both hold.
Ran the definition-of-done command `uv run ruff check research/o008_e011_diag`: all checks passed. The deliverable file exists.
caveats: The root cause and its class hold: the search stops short of moves that both L1 and L2 rate as improving, a reach failure. So does the recommended move-set change. The mechanism breakdown does not. The slot1_u0/row_LS_u0 coupled DRC wall also traps draws 0 and 4, so coupled blocks explain four of the six misses, not two.

The case for a 2 mm L1 screen is weaker than the diagnosis states. At 2 mm, the end points of draws 7 and 6 are still local minima along row_LS_u0 with the wrong sign. Escaping them depends on the proposed line moves, not on the mesh. Whether 2 mm is the right hmax, as opposed to 1.5 mm, is open.

As written, option A's coupled-move rule fires only on rejected ±0.5 mm single moves. It may not free draw 0, where the valid single step is L1-uphill at 4 mm, unless it also covers rejected line moves.
The counterfactual evidence is single structured moves solved at 0.5 mm. Nothing shows that a full redesigned search reaches these points or that they hold at 0.25 mm. §9 acknowledges both limits.

Bash denied several of my read-only inspection scripts, which looked like pattern-triggered denials. I did not inspect t3_l1_paths.json, t3b_dierow_scans.json or t6_sensitivity.json directly, and the T3a/T3b/T6 numbers were not re-verified beyond the overlapping checks listed.
